original_question: Do there exist infinitely many strongly regular geodetic graphs, or any strongly regular geodetic graphs that are not Moore graphs?
target_in_paper: B. Open Problems Related to Construction and Enumeration, open problem 4: 'Do there exist infinitely many strongly regular geodetic graphs, or any strongly regular geodetic graphs that are not Moore graphs?' ([dizzw.com](https://dizzw.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/07/Deutsche-internationale-Zeitschrift-f%C3%BCr-zeitgen%C3%B6ssische-Wissenschaft-%E2%84%9636-2022.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft matches the paper's official formulation almost verbatim and preserves its exact two-part existence scope: asking both about infinitely many strongly regular geodetic graphs and about the existence of any such graph that is not a Moore graph. ([dizzw.com](https://dizzw.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/07/Deutsche-internationale-Zeitschrift-f%C3%BCr-zeitgen%C3%B6ssische-Wissenschaft-%E2%84%9636-2022.pdf))
missing_details: Define 'geodetic graph' as a graph in which every pair of distinct vertices has a unique geodesic, i.e. a unique shortest path between them. ([dizzw.com](https://dizzw.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/07/Deutsche-internationale-Zeitschrift-f%C3%BCr-zeitgen%C3%B6ssische-Wissenschaft-%E2%84%9636-2022.pdf))

Define 'strongly regular graph' as a k-regular graph for which there exist integers λ and μ such that adjacent vertices have exactly λ common neighbors and nonadjacent vertices have exactly μ common neighbors. ([dizzw.com](https://dizzw.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/07/Deutsche-internationale-Zeitschrift-f%C3%BCr-zeitgen%C3%B6ssische-Wissenschaft-%E2%84%9636-2022.pdf))

Define 'Moore graph' in the paper's sense as a regular graph of degree k and diameter d satisfying |V(G)| = 1 + k Σ_{j=1}^d (k - 1)^{j - 1}. ([dizzw.com](https://dizzw.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/07/Deutsche-internationale-Zeitschrift-f%C3%BCr-zeitgen%C3%B6ssische-Wissenschaft-%E2%84%9636-2022.pdf))

Make explicit that this is a pure graph-theoretic existence question over graphs G; the paper introduces no ambient ring/field, operator, homogeneity, nilpotency, or 'for all sufficiently large m' clause here. ([dizzw.com](https://dizzw.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/07/Deutsche-internationale-Zeitschrift-f%C3%BCr-zeitgen%C3%B6ssische-Wissenschaft-%E2%84%9636-2022.pdf))
refined_question: Do there exist infinitely many graphs G that are both geodetic and strongly regular, where geodetic means that every pair of distinct vertices of G is joined by a unique geodesic and strongly regular means that G is k-regular with integers λ and μ such that adjacent vertices have exactly λ common neighbors and nonadjacent vertices have exactly μ common neighbors; or does there exist at least one such graph G that is not a Moore graph, meaning a regular graph of degree k and diameter d with |V(G)| = 1 + k Σ_{j=1}^d (k - 1)^{j - 1}? ([dizzw.com](https://dizzw.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/07/Deutsche-internationale-Zeitschrift-f%C3%BCr-zeitgen%C3%B6ssische-Wissenschaft-%E2%84%9636-2022.pdf))
justification: The draft is already aimed at the exact place in the paper: item 4 under 'B. Open Problems Related to Construction and Enumeration.' The only additions needed to make it fully stand-alone are the local definitions immediately given on the preceding page for geodetic graph, strongly regular graph, and Moore graph. The paper does not attach extra hypotheses such as homeomorphism to a given graph, diameter restriction, clique exclusion, or block assumptions to item 4 itself, so the refined version should remain exactly this narrow and no broader. ([dizzw.com](https://dizzw.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/07/Deutsche-internationale-Zeitschrift-f%C3%BCr-zeitgen%C3%B6ssische-Wissenschaft-%E2%84%9636-2022.pdf))
